scenes.script_line: This is the turning point of the whole process. You've seen the old story clearly. Now you get to write a new one. In step seven, you'll create a new story that is fully aligned with what matters most to you, and with everything you wrote in step one. Why write a whole story, and not just a single positive sentence? Because a single sentence is easy to dismiss. A story has depth. It has reasons, feelings, and a direction. It gives your mind somewhere new to live.

scenes.script_line: It can help to give your new story a simple shape. Begin with what's true now. Bring in the evidence you found in step six. Describe who you are, using "I am." Then describe where you're going, connected to step one. And end with a clear commitment. Page fifteen gives you seven tips. Get it done. Let go into the process, and allow yourself to write it. It's inspiring. Your new story should excite and inspire you when you read it. Mission. Connect it to the bigger direction you wrote in step one. Why. Let yourself feel why this new story matters as you write it. Positive. Write in positive, for

scenes.script_line: Those last two matter. "I am" speaks to identity. "The truth is" anchors the story in reality, not wishful thinking. Together, they keep your story both inspiring and believable. When you write "the truth is," you're inviting yourself to check that what follows really is true. And when you write "I am," you're stepping into it, now, rather than someday.

scenes.script_line: Here's part of Sam's new story. "The truth is, I've been leading for years, I just didn't call it that. I am someone people trust and listen to. I am learning, and I grow into every challenge I take on. The truth is, confidence comes from doing, and I am doing it. I am ready to lead a team I'm proud of, and I'm going for the role." Notice that it's not fantasy. Every line connects to real evidence from step six. That's what makes a new story believable, and lasting.

scenes.script_line: Watch for three common traps. The first is being too vague. "I am great" doesn't give your mind anything to hold on to. The second is being too grand. If you don't believe a line when you read it, rewrite it until you do. And the third is writing what you think you should want. This is your story. It should sound like you.

scenes.script_line: Like the old story, you can write as many drafts as you need. Use the extra space on page fifteen. Then, when you're ready, write your final version on page sixteen. Read it back out loud when you've finished. If it doesn't move you yet, keep going. Change a word. Add a reason. Bring in another piece of evidence. You'll know it's ready when reading it makes you sit up a little straighter. Your facilitator is here to help you shape it.
